title: Man. Post. Cap. X: PLAC retorsion — swap in inherent original vice; that is the pre-law sin
pass_a_gloss: So your proposition hangs on that prior argumentation, which Cap. IX already riddled with many shafts. Placeus may lawfully swap in: inherent original vice in all is the sin of the prior verse. Therefore the pre-law world-sin is that inherent original vice—which he not only admits but contends is imputed to all unless forgiven through Christ.
pass_b_english: Therefore this proposition of yours rests on your prior argumentation, which you see riddled and finished by us in the preceding chapter with many shafts, so that by my right I may put this in its place: But original vice inherent in all men is that sin of which the Apostle spoke in the immediately preceding verse, as I proved above.
Therefore that sin which was in the world until the law is original vice inherent in all, which vice I not only confess but even contend is to be imputed to all, unless it is forgiven through Christ.
source_text: Nititur igitur haec tua propositio superiori tua argumentatione, quam vides a nobis capite praecedente multis telis confossam ac confectam, ut iure meo possim eius loco hanc ponere, Atqui vitium originale omnibus hominibus inhaerens est illud peccatum de quo loquutus est Apostolus versu immediate praecedenti, ut supra probavi. Ergo peccatum illud quod fuit in mundo usque ad legem est vitium originale omnibus inhaerens, quod vitium omnibus, nisi condonetur per Christum, imputari non fateor modo, sed contendo etiam.

choices.choice: Swap inherent original vice; still imputed unless forgiven
